notes: **2026-08-31** — (branch `fix/B199-merge-lock-scope-decision`, off master `da8a61b6`; no schema change) — **B199 merge-lock scope: DEFERRED ON EVIDENCE, not left dangling.** `@routeflow/api` runs exactly ONE instance — no `numReplicas` in `apps/api/railway.toml`, `numReplicas = null` for every service in Railway's API (no dashboard override), live deployment reports 1 running instance — so `withOrderMergeLock`'s per-process scope is sufficient and the cross-replica lost update is UNREACHABLE. Restructuring `updateOrderItems` (money-critical) to close an unreachable race was judged the larger risk. ⚠️ The trigger is SCALING and it is SILENT — wrong money with no error, log or failing test — and Railway injects no replica-count variable, so nothing in-process can detect it; the guard is therefore a comment in `apps/api/railway.toml`'s `[deploy]` block, at the point the decision is made. Three designs recorded in `withOrderMergeLock`'s doc comment, cheapest first: Redis lock (Redis already a dependency, smallest diff, keeps the T-B199 spec's one-instance framing valid), optimistic CAS + 409 retry, then the full fold-inside-the-transaction (which requires MOVING, never deleting, the spec's "two concurrent merges on ONE INSTANCE serialize" block). || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
